To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

water-saving irrigation techniques such as continuous standing water and intermittent irrigation, combined with direct wet- or dry-seeded establishment, can reduce irrigation water inputs by 20–40%, while retaining high yields.

(i) wet-seeded rice can be an effective strategy to reduce water use and maintain high yields, and (ii) shallow groundwater tables reduce the potential for saving water and increase the risk of yield loss.

(i) direct wet-seeded and dry-seeded rice can save 19% of irrigation water and increase water productivity by 30% in comparison with traditional transplanted flooded rice; (ii) keeping the soil continuously at saturation reduces irrigation water input by 35% compared with continuous flooding; (iii) the potential for saving irrigation water is greater in wet-seeded than in transplanted rice, and (iv) shallow groundwater depth increases the possibility of reducing irrigation water input and saving water
